correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the Euclidean Steiner normalization on the q+1 dimensional incidence span. A selected incidence-column set is independent iff it is a forest; the squared Gram determinant is the product of sizes of its nontrivial tree components by Cauchy–Binet. In K_{2,q} at most one peripheral vertex may attach to both hubs, giving exact disconnected two-star and connected one-tree counts and the stated V_k for every k including 0 and q+1. With three-state probability t/(1+2t), multinomial Taylor expansion gives the first contribution (p/2)q+O_t(1); the single-bridge binomial term yields C_t q^(3/2)+O_t(sqrt(q)). Its sqrt(H+3) tilt changes total variation by O_t(q^-1/2), proving the displayed binomial and Gaussian laws for fixed t>0. Independently constructed signed incidence matrices for q=2,3,4, enumerated all edge subsets, computed exact Gram determinants, and matched every nonzero determinant multiplicity; finite cases are not the unrestricted proof.
